findings.claim: A rejected creation is cached as an error; clones share the complete entry-point outcome and every cache lookup retains rejection.
findings.mismatch: Progress is deliberately returned outside CachedPipeline, removes the prior DeviceHandled entry, and may itself retain a captured native rejection. That result is neither cached nor shared by later lookup. The unchanged broad comments now conflict with this intended progress/cache contract, correctly described in the guide.
findings.remedy: Qualify these comments: completed native validation outcomes are shared, including native rejection; progress failures remain uncached and retryable. Error type documentation should promise retained cause ownership rather than every lookup receiving every rejection.
findings.acceptance: Public docs distinguish cached observed native outcomes from uncached observation failures without suggesting a retry is guaranteed to succeed.

resolved.evidence: deformation.rs now says other bindings retain their own allocation ranges, correctly including renderer-owned binding6 parameters.

verified_contracts: ValidationScope::finish attempts one native wait then explicitly pops/reads scope even on returned poll Err. ValidationProgressError retains actual PollError and optional wgpu Error. When both exist standard source prioritizes native, while poll remains a concrete public field; no fabricated error parsing.

ErrorScopeGuard makes ValidationScope same-thread and non-Send/non-Sync. Implicit drop pops/discards through SDK guard; only explicit finish observes results. No scope is held across await in these new paths.

No explicit SDK timeout requested; backend-returned poll failures still escape. Successful polling is not global health. Existing construction/record waits can wait latest submission observed when poll starts; later work is not certified.

Native-only observation maps back to existing Native variants and identical diagnostic prefixes/direct wgpu Error source. Progress has a separate typed payload and view operation/original request. Generic constructor/face errors retain native root causes through existing anyhow context prefixes.

ComputePassError::resolve_observation is called after scope finish; both error values are retained, the operation remains primary Error::source, and additional observation accessible by typed field. Operation-only results retain the original error.

Pipeline progress returns before cache insertion and before new compilation state publication. Earlier DeviceHandled same-entry cache is removed; observed native rejection still cached; existing observed successful/rejected entries remain shared. Device-handled Ok remains no synchronous validation verdict.

Texture matching-format cache branch priority, MissingView/Uninitialized messages, supplied device checks, linear storage format mapping, original request, descriptors/dimensions/layers/labels and Arc sharing remain unchanged. Cached returns bypass polling.
Static uniforms observe allocation before upload; they do not map rejected allocation. No operation-plus-observation cause is silently discarded by resolver.

Converter keeps creating-device provenance, source-before-destination missing cache order and current selected views, fixed unfilterable load-only input. Scope is read after finish and again after queue submission; second progress error can follow submission, no rollback guarantee.

Guide correctly keeps recorded commands, consumed arena slots and already submitted conversion work distinct from rollback, completion and global health. WgpuContext submit remains no-wait native Validation observation, separate from construction/record ValidationScope waits.
Browser and borrowed configured paths install no new synchronous scope, and canonical shader parsing remains separate. Existing completion docs retain callback-only WebGPU limitation.
